# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **When there's nothing left to do, say so boldly at the end of the conversation.** Don't bury a "this is complete / I'm blocked / nothing further to do" behind hedging — make the terminal state unmistakable. **Set it apart visually so it catches the eye:** put the terminal state — or, when work remains, the list of open/outstanding items — in its own callout (a Markdown blockquote box, e.g. `> ✅ All done` or `> ⚠️ Still open: …`), not trailing prose the owner has to scan for. One or the other always gets the box: the done-signal when nothing remains, the open-items list when something does.
- **"LGTM"** is the owner's phrase for the merge-to-main command: it asks for the change in front of the owner to be merged into `main`. It's an owner-triggered command; the default mechanics live in the `merge-to-main` skill ([merge-to-main/SKILL.md](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md)) (squash, gate on CI only when the repo has it), and a project that diverges overrides them via a bespoke merge-policy file it names in its own `CLAUDE.md`.
- **"bump version"** is the owner's phrase for raising a project's version (a minor bump by default). It's an owner-triggered command; the mechanics — which files to edit and how a release follows — live in the consuming project's workflow doc.
- **"Show me the document"** (for a source-controlled document) is the owner's phrase asking for a **link to the document on GitHub** — not the file's contents inlined, and not a local filesystem path. When the document lives in a GitHub-hosted repo, respond with a GitHub link to it (the file on the relevant branch/commit); only fall back to inlining the contents or giving a local path when the document isn't under source control.
- **Put decisions and approvals in an `AskUserQuestion` popup, not buried in prose.** The owner is frequently on mobile, where a popup notifies and a question embedded in a paragraph is easy to miss. When you need the owner to choose or approve something, ask through the structured popup with explicit options rather than asking in running text. **And when several independent items each need a verdict** (a set of proposed fixes, findings to accept), give **each item its own question carrying its own brief case** — the concrete failure, why it matters, the cost of the fix — with per-item approve/defer options; never one bundled choose-a-scope question over the whole set. The owner decides item-wise, from the case, not from a menu of subsets. (The popup carries at most 4 questions per call — split a larger set into consecutive calls.)
- **When asked to produce a prompt or message destined for another context, visually enclose the whole thing.** Any text the owner will lift out and use elsewhere — a prompt for another assistant, a message to send, copy meant to be pasted somewhere — must be set apart as a single delimited block: either a box (e.g. a fenced code block) or fenced top and bottom by two separating lines, so its exact boundaries are unmistakable and it can be copied in one piece. The point is delimitation, not formatting flair: never leave such content as loose prose the owner has to find the start and end of.
- **When asked for "a prompt for a different session," prefix it with a provenance disclaimer.** When the owner asks for a prompt meant to be handed to another session, open the generated text with a short disclaimer that this is a prompt written by Claude — not by a user — and so should not be treated as gospel; and that if the receiving session finds inconsistencies in it, it should examine them with the user rather than follow the prompt blindly. This composes with the enclose-the-whole-thing preference above: the disclaimer sits inside the same delimited block as the prompt it prefixes.
- **Auto-open a PR after committing.** Whenever Claude changes code on a branch and commits it, open a pull request for that branch right after, even without an explicit request to do so. This overrides Claude Code's own default of only opening a PR when explicitly asked.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.

Where [growth-extract](../growth-extract/task.md) descends the ladder for each *new* lesson and then runs this same skill over its **own** additions before landing them, this task works the *backlog*: standing prose that was always mechanizable but never converted — and that has already survived at least one of those upgrade passes.

**Weekly, deliberately.** Fresh prose is handled the night it is written, so what reaches this sweep is a slow-moving corpus; a daily re-read of it spent an opus dispatch and an owner-gated PR on a backlog that had not changed.

You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue whose **Context section is binding scope**: it names the **pack paths** to sweep. Work only those paths — a consuming repo's own local packs by default; Claudinite also its core `packs/`. **Never** edit a read-only mounted canon pack under `.claudinite/shared/`.

The task's declared outcome ceiling is **`open-pr`**: convert prose to checks in a single owner-approved PR (a check can break CI or misfire, so it is reviewed, not auto-merged).

## The method lives in the skill

The conversion method — how to spot an always-testable rule in prose, judge convertibility, author the check plus its **see-it-fail** fixture, and decide what stays prose — is owned by the [**prose-to-checks** skill](../../skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md). Follow it; don't re-derive it here. This worker only frames the unattended run around it.

## What a run does

1. **Pick convertible prose** under the Context's pack paths — rules that govern **how we work** (not what the product does — see the skill's first gate), that are *always testable* (a deterministic condition a check could assert), and that no existing check already covers. Prefer the strongest, clearest candidates; converting one or two solid rules well beats churning many shakily.

Then apply the skill's **deletion test** to the prose the check now stands beside — a paragraph the check fully covers is deleted whole, never trimmed.

4. **Log to the tracker** — the standing log is the issue titled exactly **`Claudinite tracker: Prose to Checks`** in this repo. Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number**; create it already closed if missing. **Never open, close, or reopen it**. Log each run as a **dated comment**: the prose converted and the check id it became, or "nothing convertible this run".

## What this task must never do

- **Never ship a check that can't be made confident** — the see-it-fail fixture is the gate; an unprovable rule stays prose.
- **Never convert a rule an existing check already covers** — dedupe against the check set first.
- **Never convert a statement of what the product does** — a rule asserting which entities exist, what a surface renders, or that a feature's parts are wired together is a **requirement**, and belongs in the project's executable spec and the suite that proves it. Such a rule is testable, so it passes the check-the-world test on its own; the skill's first gate is what stops it. Found in pack prose it is already mis-homed — leave it and log it, never cement it as a check.
- **Never touch a pack path outside the Context**, and **never edit a mounted canon pack** under `.claudinite/shared/` — a consumer improves only its own local packs.

5	
6	# Convert existing prose to checks
7	
8	A completeness-critic over a repo's own packs: prose that is always-testable but was never converted
9	becomes a check, so the packs keep shedding context over time instead of only at the moment a rule is
10	first learned.
11	
12	## Two callers, differing only in scope
13	
14	- **The upgrade pass**, as the last step of a
15	  [growth-extract](../../tasks/growth-extract/task.md) run: the scope is the prose **that run just
16	  wrote**. Extraction already descends the promotion ladder per lesson, but a lesson written as prose
17	  under time pressure is exactly where a convertible rule hides, so it gets asked once more before the
18	  PR opens. Never widen from here into the standing backlog.

21	  passes in its Context. A consuming repo's own **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/`) by

23	  `packs/`. Read the prose under those paths (each pack's `RULES.md`, and any `SKILL.md` beside them).
24	
25	Plus on demand, when someone asks. Either way: never edit a read-only mounted canon pack under
26	`.claudinite/shared/`. Everything below is identical for both callers.
27	
28	## First gate — a working rule, not a product statement
29	
30	Before asking whether a rule is *testable*, ask whether it belongs to a pack at all: **does it govern
31	how we work, or state what the product does?** A pack — canon or local — homes the conventions,
32	gotchas and review discipline that recur across tasks whatever the feature happens to be. A rule
33	asserting which entities exist, what a surface must render, or that a feature's parts are wired to
34	each other is a **requirement**; its home is the project's executable spec and the suite that proves
35	it (the full rule lives in
36	[generate-project-instructions](../generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md)).
37	
38	This gate comes **first** because product statements sail through the check-the-world test below —
39	"this module must export `X`" has an obvious static signature. Converting one splits a feature's
40	definition across two systems and lands half of it in the one no test of the product ever reads.
41	Load-bearingness is not the test: a real gap in product coverage is a *requirements* gap.
42	
43	A product statement already sitting in pack prose is mis-homed, and a sweep is not the place to
44	re-home it. **Leave the prose and log it** as a mis-homed rule, the same way an un-checkable
45	candidate is logged — never cement it as a check.
46	
47	## What to look for — the check-the-world test
48	
49	For each rule that cleared the gate, ask the one question from
50	[engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md): **does it constrain a *static
51	signature in the repo artifact* — something a post-hoc scan could observe?**
52	
53	- **Yes → a conversion candidate.** A dangling-reference rule, a filename convention, a workflow
54	  or manifest shape, a "these two files must agree" invariant, a forbidden pattern in code.
55	- **No → leave it.** In-flight process (leaves no artifact — "see the test fail first"),
56	  judgment ("name by scope"), or knowledge whose failure is only visible at runtime (jsdom
57	  diverging from Chrome). These are why the rule is prose; don't force them.
58	
59	**A static signature is necessary, not sufficient.** Both shapes the working-discipline rules bar
60	— a rule that pins today's code in place, and one derivable from the product's requirements —
61	answer *yes* here, so screen every candidate against that bar before converting it. Leave either
62	where it is; routing a requirement to the spec and its suite is its own change, not this sweep's.
63	
64	The check-the-world rule from DESIGN holds: if a rule is always-testable, it was never really
65	part of the on-demand skill — it belongs in a pack as a check.
66	
67	## How to convert one
68	
69	Follow the extract stage's check-authoring discipline (the local promotion ladder in
70	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). For each candidate:
71	
72	> **The upgrade-pass caller lands inside growth-extract's own PR**, which auto-merges after CI — so the
73	> see-it-fail fixture is the only gate a converted check gets there. Convert only what you can prove;
74	> anything shakier stays prose and waits for the weekly sweep's reviewed PR.
75	
76	1. **Author the check** in the owning pack (`<pack>/<rule>.mjs`, listed in its `pack.mjs`) — the
77	   failure message *is* the rule (what / why / fix / `doc:` pointer back to the prose).
78	2. **Write the fixture first and see it fail** — a violating fixture must find, a clean one must
79	   not (the test lives beside the pack's other tests). A conversion with no proving fixture
80	   doesn't ship.
81	3. **Ship at real severity, fail-fast** — blocking for a defect, advisory only when the rule is
82	   directional by kind.
83	4. **Delete the prose the check now covers** — whole, never trimmed. The deletion test below is
84	   how you decide which paragraphs those are.
85	
86	**Before writing a rule off as un-checkable, try parsing the file's structure instead of grepping
87	its text.** Grep finds the pattern anywhere; parsing finds it in the one spot the rule means —
88	which kills the false alarm. (Example: `Authorization` is only wrong inside a CloudFront policy's
89	*own* header list, not elsewhere in the template.) Parse only as much as you need, and hold the
90	check to the same fixture bar.
91	
92	When even a scoped parser can't make detection confident, **leave the prose and log the
93	candidate** to a tagged conversion-backlog issue rather than shipping a shaky check.
94	
95	## Coming out: the deletion test
96	
97	Coming out of a conversion, apply the **deletion test**: prose a mechanism fully covers is
98	deleted, never trimmed. Ask it of every paragraph standing beside a landed check — *with this
99	paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it describes **and** tell the agent
100	how to fix it?* If yes, it is redundant: delete it whole. The check's failure message is where
101	the rule lives now and its header comment is where the rationale lives, so a paragraph restating
102	either pays twice and is the drift trap waiting to spring.
103	
104	Before concluding prose is the only carrier, look at the pack's **skills** too — an
105	activity-scoped skill often already holds the map a rule is repeating. Keep only what no artifact
106	carries.
107	
108	The test **discriminates** rather than just deleting: a paragraph stays whole whenever it carries
109	something the check does not — a second rule in the same breath, an exemption the check can't
110	encode, a value the check can't judge, or a remedy the finding's own `fix` line never states
111	(a finding renders `what` / `why` / `fix` / `doc`, never the rule's `description`, so a remedy
112	that lives only in the description is not carried). Two worked calls: an `npm test` invariant

114	while an `extension-test/` mirror bullet stayed, because the check beside it enforced only the
115	`package.json` list's sync with the tree and never the mirror convention itself.
116	
117	Whether a check covers a rule is a judgment about meaning, so this test is applied by a

  passes in its Context. A consuming repo's own **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/`) by
  default — projects don't improve core canon packs — while **Claudinite itself** also sweeps its core
  `packs/`. Read the prose under those paths (each pack's `RULES.md`, and any `SKILL.md` beside them).

Plus on demand, when someone asks. Either way: never edit a read-only mounted canon pack under
`.claudinite/shared/`. Everything below is identical for both callers.

## First gate — a working rule, not a product statement

Before asking whether a rule is *testable*, ask whether it belongs to a pack at all: **does it govern
how we work, or state what the product does?** A pack — canon or local — homes the conventions,
gotchas and review discipline that recur across tasks whatever the feature happens to be. A rule
asserting which entities exist, what a surface must render, or that a feature's parts are wired to
each other is a **requirement**; its home is the project's executable spec and the suite that proves
it (the full rule lives in
[generate-project-instructions](../generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md)).

This gate comes **first** because product statements sail through the check-the-world test below —
"this module must export `X`" has an obvious static signature. Converting one splits a feature's
definition across two systems and lands half of it in the one no test of the product ever reads.
Load-bearingness is not the test: a real gap in product coverage is a *requirements* gap.

A product statement already sitting in pack prose is mis-homed, and a sweep is not the place to
re-home it. **Leave the prose and log it** as a mis-homed rule, the same way an un-checkable
candidate is logged — never cement it as a check.

## What to look for — the check-the-world test

For each rule that cleared the gate, ask the one question from
[engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md): **does it constrain a *static
signature in the repo artifact* — something a post-hoc scan could observe?**

- **Yes → a conversion candidate.** A dangling-reference rule, a filename convention, a workflow
  or manifest shape, a "these two files must agree" invariant, a forbidden pattern in code.
- **No → leave it.** In-flight process (leaves no artifact — "see the test fail first"),
  judgment ("name by scope"), or knowledge whose failure is only visible at runtime (jsdom
  diverging from Chrome). These are why the rule is prose; don't force them.

**A static signature is necessary, not sufficient.** Both shapes the working-discipline rules bar
— a rule that pins today's code in place, and one derivable from the product's requirements —
answer *yes* here, so screen every candidate against that bar before converting it. Leave either
where it is; routing a requirement to the spec and its suite is its own change, not this sweep's.

The check-the-world rule from DESIGN holds: if a rule is always-testable, it was never really
part of the on-demand skill — it belongs in a pack as a check.

## How to convert one

Follow the extract stage's check-authoring discipline (the local promotion ladder in
[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). For each candidate:

> **The upgrade-pass caller lands inside growth-extract's own PR**, which auto-merges after CI — so the
> see-it-fail fixture is the only gate a converted check gets there. Convert only what you can prove;
> anything shakier stays prose and waits for the weekly sweep's reviewed PR.

1. **Author the check** in the owning pack (`<pack>/<rule>.mjs`, listed in its `pack.mjs`) — the
   failure message *is* the rule (what / why / fix / `doc:` pointer back to the prose).
2. **Write the fixture first and see it fail** — a violating fixture must find, a clean one must
   not (the test lives beside the pack's other tests). A conversion with no proving fixture
   doesn't ship.
3. **Ship at real severity, fail-fast** — blocking for a defect, advisory only when the rule is
   directional by kind.
4. **Delete the prose the check now covers** — whole, never trimmed. The deletion test below is
   how you decide which paragraphs those are.

**Before writing a rule off as un-checkable, try parsing the file's structure instead of grepping
its text.** Grep finds the pattern anywhere; parsing finds it in the one spot the rule means —
which kills the false alarm. (Example: `Authorization` is only wrong inside a CloudFront policy's
*own* header list, not elsewhere in the template.) Parse only as much as you need, and hold the
check to the same fixture bar.

When even a scoped parser can't make detection confident, **leave the prose and log the
candidate** to a tagged conversion-backlog issue rather than shipping a shaky check.

## Coming out: the deletion test

Coming out of a conversion, apply the **deletion test**: prose a mechanism fully covers is
deleted, never trimmed. Ask it of every paragraph standing beside a landed check — *with this
paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it describes **and** tell the agent
how to fix it?* If yes, it is redundant: delete it whole. The check's failure message is where
the rule lives now and its header comment is where the rationale lives, so a paragraph restating
either pays twice and is the drift trap waiting to spring.

Before concluding prose is the only carrier, look at the pack's **skills** too — an
activity-scoped skill often already holds the map a rule is repeating. Keep only what no artifact
carries.

The test **discriminates** rather than just deleting: a paragraph stays whole whenever it carries
something the check does not — a second rule in the same breath, an exemption the check can't
encode, a value the check can't judge, or a remedy the finding's own `fix` line never states
(a finding renders `what` / `why` / `fix` / `doc`, never the rule's `description`, so a remedy
that lives only in the description is not carried). Two worked calls: an `npm test` invariant
went entirely — the check caught it and the testing-guide skill already listed the suites —
while an `extension-test/` mirror bullet stayed, because the check beside it enforced only the
`package.json` list's sync with the tree and never the mirror convention itself.

Whether a check covers a rule is a judgment about meaning, so this test is applied by a
**reader**, not mechanized.

## Bounds

- **One PR, bounded surface** — the new rule module, its `pack.mjs` line, its fixture, and the
  trimmed prose. Don't "improve" unrelated rules while you're in there.
- **Never delete a rule you didn't convert** — the deletion test is only ever asked of a rule a
  *landed* check now enforces.
- Run the suite and the sweep green before the PR goes up, and never push to `main` directly. The
  sweep opens its own PR for the owner's approval; the upgrade pass adds its conversion to the
  growth-extract PR already being opened, and opens none of its own.

Same for the pending-page sweep: the pages that did record still land. - **The generic-coverage gate is a high-watermark over a changing case set.** A removed/renamed case the watermark still lists makes it stale: the local refresh re-anchors it (commit that); in CI it's an error to fix. *Caveat:* never commit a re-anchored baseline while the gate is red — a regression bundled with a case-set change can be re-anchored over. Detailed mechanics self-document in the gate's own headers (`dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.js` / `.test.js`). - **To see what the core generic extractor gets ON ITS OWN** on any cached page — even a supported host — load the files, set `GCal.sources = []`, then call `GCal.extract()`: the documented way to strip every per-site override and see the bare base through the same norm/sort the popup uses. (`GCal.extract()` alone no longer answers this: the generic extractor is the base layer of every extraction now, so on a supported host its output already carries the site's overrides.) Most start/end *differences* vs a dedicated source are just its hardcoded `ctz` localizing to floating time (same instant), not extraction bugs; the real gaps are fields it can't know generically (durations, site-specific descriptions, and — where the page doesn't declare corroborating hints, see `helpers/derive-timezone.js` — `ctz`). This is the comparison the generic-coverage gate automates — and a case where it shows NO gap is a candidate for deleting the per-site source and listing the host in `supportedDomains`). ## Architecture rules of the road Whenever we agree on a new or changed top-level architectural guideline, update this section as part of the same change (the design doc itself is `dev/procedures/highLevelDesign.md`): - **`extension/event-extractors/custom/` is the extensibility point — one file per site, and nothing else.** The rest of `event-extractors/` is the pipeline itself: the registry, the orchestrator, the shared helpers, and the one core generic extractor (`generic-extractor.js`), which is a different kind of thing from a per-site file. - **The core generic extractor is the base layer of every extraction** — it runs on every page, and a per-site source is only a layer of *overrides* merged over it, stating the fields it gets better. A source never re-reads what the page already says about itself, and the generic extractor may never know about a specific site. - **Being supported is DECLARED, never derived from the extractors.** `supportedDomains` in `extension/host-lists.json` is the one list of hosts we claim, read directly by the toolbar worker and the popup. Never add a second list, and never register a placeholder source just to make a host count as supported. The only guarded direction is that every per-site source's host appears in the list. - **A site we fully support gets no extractor file when there is nothing to override.** It stays listed in `supportedDomains` and stays fully supported — green icon, no correction prompt — with no file at all. When a `custom/.js` shrinks to nothing, just delete it; when such a site starts needing a fix the generic extractor can't make site-agnostically, add the file back. Never keep a file whose only content is a restatement of the generic base, and never annotate one as "nothing to add". - Adding support for a new host is the most common change — the architecture must keep it a single-file change: a host added to `supportedDomains`, plus — only when the generic extractor gets that site wrong — one self-contained new `extension/event-extractors/custom/.js` and a regenerated load list, touching nothing else and assuming nothing about other extractors. ## Capture policy — lessons land in the local packs **The gcec local pack is this repo's capture surface.** Route each lesson to its section here: extractor-automation to the "Extractor pipeline" section, everything else to the fitting section. Mechanism before prose, per the canon's local promotion ladder — `test-offline-list-sync` is this pack's worked example. **Three kinds never land here, however strong the evidence** — filter on what a lesson is *about* before picking a mechanism: - **The owner's personal preferences** (which word means "merge it", tone, summary style). 36	const why =
37	  'node --test never errors on a glob that matches nothing — a test file no pattern ' +
38	  'reaches silently never runs, and npm test still exits 0';

40	const isTestFile = (p) => /\.test\.(js|mjs|cjs)$/.test(p);
41	
42	// The file/glob arguments of a `node --test …` script line. Quotes come off (the
43	// globs are quoted so the shell can't expand them first); the binary and every
44	// flag drop out. A leftover non-pattern token can only ever fail to match, which
45	// under-reports rather than false-alarms.
46	function runnerPatterns(script) {
47	  if (typeof script !== 'string') return [];
48	  if (!/(^|\s)--test(\s|$)/.test(script)) return []; // not a glob-driven runner
49	  return script
50	    .split(/\s+/)
51	    .map((t) => t.replace(/^['"]/, '').replace(/['"]$/, ''))
52	    .filter((t) => t && t !== 'node' && !t.startsWith('-'));
53	}
54	
55	const ESCAPE_RE = /[.+^${}()|[\]\\]/g;
56	const STAR_STAR = '\u0000'; // placeholder for a whole `**` path segment
57	
58	// A minimal glob → matcher for those patterns, applied per path segment so `**`
59	// is only special as a segment of its own: `**` spans directories, `*` and `?`
60	// stay inside one segment. A pattern carrying no wildcard and no file extension
61	// is a DIRECTORY argument — `node --test <dir>` recurses — so it covers
62	// everything beneath it.
63	function toMatcher(pattern) {
64	  const p = pattern.replace(/\/+$/, '');
65	  if (!/[*?]/.test(p) && !/\.[a-z0-9]+$/i.test(p)) {
66	    return (f) => f === p || f.startsWith(`${p}/`);
67	  }
68	  const source = p
69	    .split('/')
70	    .map((seg) =>
71	      seg === '**'
72	        ? STAR_STAR
73	        : seg.replace(ESCAPE_RE, '\\$&').replace(/\*/g, '[^/]*').replace(/\?/g, '[^/]'),
74	    )
75	    .join('/')
76	    // A leading `**/` matches ZERO or more directories — that's what makes
77	    // extension-test/**/*.test.js cover extension-test/host-policy.test.js too.
78	    .split(`${STAR_STAR}/`)
79	    .join('(?:.*/)?')
80	    .split(`/${STAR_STAR}`)
81	    .join('(?:/.*)?')
82	    .split(STAR_STAR)
83	    .join('.*');
84	  const re = new RegExp(`^${source}$`);
85	  return (f) => re.test(f);
86	}

89	const anyMatch = (ms, file) => ms.some((m) => m(file));

94	  description: "package.json's test script globs reach every committed test file",

96	  why,

50	[engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md): **does it constrain a *static
51	signature in the repo artifact* — something a post-hoc scan could observe?**
52	
53	- **Yes → a conversion candidate.** A dangling-reference rule, a filename convention, a workflow
54	  or manifest shape, a "these two files must agree" invariant, a forbidden pattern in code.
55	- **No → leave it.** In-flight process (leaves no artifact — "see the test fail first"),
56	  judgment ("name by scope"), or knowledge whose failure is only visible at runtime (jsdom
57	  diverging from Chrome). These are why the rule is prose; don't force them.
58	
59	**A static signature is necessary, not sufficient.** Both shapes the working-discipline rules bar
60	— a rule that pins today's code in place, and one derivable from the product's requirements —
61	answer *yes* here, so screen every candidate against that bar before converting it. Leave either
62	where it is; routing a requirement to the spec and its suite is its own change, not this sweep's.
63	
64	The check-the-world rule from DESIGN holds: if a rule is always-testable, it was never really
65	part of the on-demand skill — it belongs in a pack as a check.
66	
67	## How to convert one
68	
69	Follow the extract stage's check-authoring discipline (the local promotion ladder in
70	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). For each candidate:
71	
72	> **The upgrade-pass caller lands inside growth-extract's own PR**, which auto-merges after CI — so the
73	> see-it-fail fixture is the only gate a converted check gets there. Convert only what you can prove;
74	> anything shakier stays prose and waits for the weekly sweep's reviewed PR.
75	
76	1. **Author the check** in the owning pack (`<pack>/<rule>.mjs`, listed in its `pack.mjs`) — the
77	   failure message *is* the rule (what / why / fix / `doc:` pointer back to the prose).
78	2. **Write the fixture first and see it fail** — a violating fixture must find, a clean one must
79	   not (the test lives beside the pack's other tests). A conversion with no proving fixture
80	   doesn't ship.
81	3. **Ship at real severity, fail-fast** — blocking for a defect, advisory only when the rule is
82	   directional by kind.
83	4. **Delete the prose the check now covers** — whole, never trimmed. The deletion test below is
84	   how you decide which paragraphs those are.
85	
86	**Before writing a rule off as un-checkable, try parsing the file's structure instead of grepping
87	its text.** Grep finds the pattern anywhere; parsing finds it in the one spot the rule means —
88	which kills the false alarm. (Example: `Authorization` is only wrong inside a CloudFront policy's
89	*own* header list, not elsewhere in the template.) Parse only as much as you need, and hold the
90	check to the same fixture bar.
91	
92	When even a scoped parser can't make detection confident, **leave the prose and log the
93	candidate** to a tagged conversion-backlog issue rather than shipping a shaky check.
94	
95	## Coming out: the deletion test
96	
97	Coming out of a conversion, apply the **deletion test**: prose a mechanism fully covers is
98	deleted, never trimmed. Ask it of every paragraph standing beside a landed check — *with this
99	paragraph gone, would the check still catch every violation it describes **and** tell the agent
100	how to fix it?* If yes, it is redundant: delete it whole. The check's failure message is where
101	the rule lives now and its header comment is where the rationale lives, so a paragraph restating
102	either pays twice and is the drift trap waiting to spring.
103	
104	Before concluding prose is the only carrier, look at the pack's **skills** too — an
105	activity-scoped skill often already holds the map a rule is repeating. Keep only what no artifact
106	carries.
107	
108	The test **discriminates** rather than just deleting: a paragraph stays whole whenever it carries
109	something the check does not — a second rule in the same breath, an exemption the check can't
110	encode, a value the check can't judge, or a remedy the finding's own `fix` line never states
111	(a finding renders `what` / `why` / `fix` / `doc`, never the rule's `description`, so a remedy
112	that lives only in the description is not carried). Two worked calls: an `npm test` invariant
113	went entirely — the check caught it and the testing-guide skill already listed the suites —
114	while an `extension-test/` mirror bullet stayed, because the check beside it enforced only the
115	`package.json` list's sync with the tree and never the mirror convention itself.
116	
117	Whether a check covers a rule is a judgment about meaning, so this test is applied by a
118	**reader**, not mechanized.
119	
120	## Bounds
121	
122	- **One PR, bounded surface** — the new rule module, its `pack.mjs` line, its fixture, and the
123	  trimmed prose. Don't "improve" unrelated rules while you're in there.
124	- **Never delete a rule you didn't convert** — the deletion test is only ever asked of a rule a
125	  *landed* check now enforces.
126	- Run the suite and the sweep green before the PR goes up, and never push to `main` directly. The
127	  sweep opens its own PR for the owner's approval; the upgrade pass adds its conversion to the
128	  growth-extract PR already being opened, and opens none of its own.

1	# Extracting lessons — the bar and the local promotion ladder
2	
3	> **Scope: what both extraction skills share.** This doc is the **bar** a lesson must clear and the
4	> **ladder** it descends once it clears it — the half that is identical whatever the lesson was mined
5	> from. What each *source* adds is owned by its own skill:
6	> [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) for commits, merged PRs and issue
7	> activity, and [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) for a session's
8	> dialogue. Both load this doc; neither restates it.
9	
10	Its callers are the growth pack's [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md) daily task, which runs
11	both skills over one window, and an owner's occasional plain-words ask for a retrospective.
12	
13	## Run the pass on a capable model
14	
15	Extraction is mechanical, but deciding *what clears the bar* is a judgment call a weaker model fails
16	silently — it ships a plausible-but-wrong "lesson" where a capable model correctly bails (see
17	[the unattended-agents skill](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md), "Match the agent model to the judgment it
18	must make"). The terse rules that *govern* the pass — run it, plus the separate efficiency analysis — also
19	live there; this doc is the how-to.
20	
21	## From signal to lesson — the bar
22	
23	A signal is only worth writing down when the fix is **durable, reusable, and generalizable beyond this one
24	session or window.** Before adding anything:
25	
26	- **Dedupe ruthlessly** against the existing packs — a lesson already covered (even worded differently,
27	  even in another pack, even enforced by a check) is not a new lesson.
28	- **One-offs don't qualify.** A situational detail, a restatement of a generic truism, or something already
29	  implied by an existing rule is below the bar.
30	- **Promote what's portable.** A lesson true for projects beyond this one belongs in shared, cross-project
31	  canon, not stuck in one repo's local packs — the growth lifecycle's promote stage lifts it there
32	  centrally; capture it well locally and let promote generalize whatever travels.
33	
34	## Route to the local pack that owns it — the promotion ladder
35	
36	A project's capture surface is its **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/`); everything else
37	under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mounted canon and is never a capture target. Pick the pack whose
38	territory the lesson belongs to (most repos have one general pack; some segregate a domain pack), then
39	prefer the strongest mechanism it allows:
40	
41	1. **A check** in that pack's rules — author the `.mjs`, list it on the pack's `pack.mjs`, ship it with a
42	   red-first fixture. Its failure message *is* the lesson.
43	2. **A pack skill**, when the lesson is an activity-scoped procedure rather than a condition.
44	3. **Terse prose** in the pack's `RULES.md` — only what neither of the above can carry.
45	
46	Write **more checks and less prose**: a check relieves every session's context completely, where prose only
47	relocates it. When no pack's scope fits and the lesson warrants segregation, a new local pack is a
48	self-contained directory drop.
49	
50	**A gotcha tied to one call site is not a pack rule at all.** A trap from misusing a specific API, class, or
51	library goes as a **comment right at the usage site** — next to the call itself, where the next editor of
52	that line sees it — never collected into a centralized gotchas list. Co-locate it in a file's own header
53	comment when the trap spans the whole file and you'd only hit it *while editing that file*. Reserve a
54	central gotchas doc for what no single usage site owns: a trap you could hit *without* reading the relevant
55	file (a mistake of omission), or a cross-cutting invariant.
56	
57	## "No new lessons" is a valid — and common — result
58	
59	Most sessions and most windows yield nothing durable, and that's the expected outcome. Say so and write
60	nothing rather than padding the docs to look productive: a spurious or duplicative "lesson" pollutes the
61	canon and costs every future reader. **Default to no edit when unsure** — the bar is a genuinely new,
62	reusable insight, not a diary of what happened.

If `regen` reports a coverage regression, that's the real gate 44 firing — review it, don't paper over it. 45 - **Keep divergence small**: when syncing a branch to `origin/main` (by rebase — 46 this repo forbids merge commits), **run `npm run regen`** as part of the sync, 47 so the branch carries freshly-generated artifacts, not just the latest 48 sources. 49 - **Whenever a change regenerates the UI gallery** (via `npm run refresh:ui`), 50 link the branch's copy in the chat in the same turn you commit it — 51 `https://github.com///blob//dev/requirements/requirements.md` 52 — for one-page review. 53 54 ## Owner commands 55 56 - **"bump version"** = cut a release **end to end** — bump, merge, and wait for 57 the published artifact. Only when the 70 owner asks — never extract unprompted. Capture routing: see below. 71 72 ## Testing invariants 73 74 - **Integration cases are the reviewed contract** — a person reads 75 `dev/requirements/extractor/expected/`; nobody reviews the unit tests. Every 76 required change or bugfix gets a case (one real, focused page per distinct 77 behavior; keep cases minimal). Unit tests under `extension-test/` are a 78 supplementary safety net for page-independent logic. 79 - **`extension-test/` mirrors `extension/`'s tree, one test per source file** 80 (`extension//.js` → `extension-test//.test.js`; the 81 path IS the link, so a source file never names its test). Deliberate 82 departures: `extension-test/integration/` for whole-extension/interaction 83 tests; no mirror for `custom/*` sources or data/markup files (covered by live 84 cases / snapshots / drift guards); `extension-test/harness.js` is shared 85 infra (not a test) and stays at the root. 86 - **The pinned `REFERENCE_NOW`** (`dev/requirements/shared/reference-time.js`, 87 currently 2026-06-01) **is the floor of the cases' dates**: author a 88 neutral/upcoming case **on or after it** so it's pill-free; use a past date or 89 a future year only when the case is *pinning* a pill. 90 91 ## Codebase gotchas 92 93 Project-wide footguns only. Portable rules these instantiate live in the canon 94 packs/skills. 95 96 - **`declarativeContent`/`UrlFilter` host-match verification is CI-only** — the 97 real URL→icon match runs inside Chrome, exercised here only by the CI-only 98 real-Chrome test (`dev/requirements/heavy/extension-load.chrome.test.js`). 99 - **CDP-introspecting the MV3 worker hits the portable traps** (canon): here 100 they bit `declarativeContent…getRules` (hung until job timeout), which is why 101 the worker publishes `globalThis.iconRulesReady` for the test to poll. 102 - **The jsdom-vs-Chrome DOM traps bit this repo directly** (canon): #130/#137 103 drove the **production** remedy the canon (framed for tests) leaves out — 104 strip `noscript`/`script`/`style` from a clone before reading any element's 105 user-facing text (the generic extractor's footer-address reader does this, #675). 106 - **Injected block markup inside a `

Never keep a file whose only content is a restatement of the generic 224 base, and never annotate one as "nothing to add". 225 - Adding support for a new host is the most common change — the architecture 226 must keep it a single-file change: a host added to `supportedDomains`, plus — 227 only when the generic extractor gets that site wrong — one self-contained new 228 `extension/event-extractors/custom/.js` and a regenerated load list, 229 touching nothing else and assuming nothing about other extractors. 230 231 ## Capture policy — lessons land in the local packs 232 233 **The gcec local pack is this repo's capture surface.** Route each lesson to its 234 section here: extractor-automation to the "Extractor pipeline" section, 235 everything else to the fitting section. Mechanism before prose, per the canon's 236 local promotion ladder — `test-offline-list-sync` is this pack's worked example. 237 238 **Three kinds never land here, however strong the evidence** — filter on what a 239 lesson is *about* before picking a mechanism: 240 241 - **The owner's personal preferences** (which word means "merge it", tone, 242 summary style). They belong to the owner, are injected per-session, and change 243 without this repo hearing about it. 244 - **Claudinite loading mechanics** (which packs are declared, why a skill didn't 245 mount, why an injection missed). Engine plumbing, not project knowledge — a 246 real defect there goes upstream instead. 247 - **Anything derived from product requirements.** Packs carry 248 **development-process** lessons only; what the extension should do is 249 `dev/requirements/`'s territory, and restating it here will drift. 250 251 None of the three is mechanically checkable, so all three stay prose. 252

1	// gcec local check: `npm test` runs everything. Its `test` script is a single
2	// `node --test` invocation over a hand-kept list of glob patterns — one per test
3	// directory — so every committed *.test.{js,mjs,cjs} in the repo must be reached
4	// by one of them. The rule this converts is RULES.md's first testing invariant
5	// ("`npm test` runs everything ... `test:e2e` (heavy, CI-only)").
6	//
7	// Why a check and not just prose: the failure is silent in exactly the way a
8	// static scan is for. A test file in a directory no pattern reaches is simply
9	// never run — `node --test` doesn't error on a glob that matches nothing, npm
10	// exits 0, CI stays green, and the coverage is just gone with nothing red to say
11	// so. The pattern list has grown one entry at a time (extension-test/,
12	// dev/build/test/, dev/build/release/, four separate dev/requirements/ subtrees,
13	// the local pack's tasks, the pack's own .mjs fixtures); the next new test
14	// directory is one forgotten glob away from that silence.
15	//
16	// The one carve-out is READ FROM package.json, never hardcoded: the heavy,
17	// CI-only e2e suite is deliberately outside `npm test`, and it declares itself
18	// in `scripts["test:e2e"]`. A file matched by that script's patterns is covered
19	// by design, so the carve-out follows the e2e suite around instead of pinning a
20	// path here.
21	//
22	// ONE DIRECTION ONLY, on purpose (the same choice as
23	// extension-test/integration/supported-domains.test.js): a *stale* pattern — one
24	// matching nothing — is not asserted, because a literal path that no longer
25	// exists makes `node --test` fail loudly on the next run. Only the silent
26	// direction needs a guard.
27	//
28	// Local-pack check modules are dependency-free on purpose (see
29	// test-offline-list-sync.mjs's header): plain finding objects, no engine imports,
30	// so they also load under the repo's own `npm test` (pack.test.mjs). The engine
31	// already drops the vendored `.claudinite/shared/` canon from ctx.files, so the
32	// canon's own tests are structurally out of scope and need no exemption here.
33	const id = 'npm-test-glob-coverage';
34	const severity = 'blocking';
35	const doc = '.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/RULES.md';
36	const why =
37	  'node --test never errors on a glob that matches nothing — a test file no pattern ' +
38	  'reaches silently never runs, and npm test still exits 0';
39	
40	const isTestFile = (p) => /\.test\.(js|mjs|cjs)$/.test(p);
41	
42	// The file/glob arguments of a `node --test …` script line. Quotes come off (the
43	// globs are quoted so the shell can't expand them first); the binary and every
44	// flag drop out. A leftover non-pattern token can only ever fail to match, which
45	// under-reports rather than false-alarms.
46	function runnerPatterns(script) {
47	  if (typeof script !== 'string') return [];
48	  if (!/(^|\s)--test(\s|$)/.test(script)) return []; // not a glob-driven runner
49	  return script
50	    .split(/\s+/)
51	    .map((t) => t.replace(/^['"]/, '').replace(/['"]$/, ''))
52	    .filter((t) => t && t !== 'node' && !t.startsWith('-'));
53	}
54	
55	const ESCAPE_RE = /[.+^${}()|[\]\\]/g;
56	const STAR_STAR = '\u0000'; // placeholder for a whole `**` path segment
57	
58	// A minimal glob → matcher for those patterns, applied per path segment so `**`
59	// is only special as a segment of its own: `**` spans directories, `*` and `?`
60	// stay inside one segment. A pattern carrying no wildcard and no file extension
61	// is a DIRECTORY argument — `node --test <dir>` recurses — so it covers
62	// everything beneath it.
63	function toMatcher(pattern) {
64	  const p = pattern.replace(/\/+$/, '');
65	  if (!/[*?]/.test(p) && !/\.[a-z0-9]+$/i.test(p)) {
66	    return (f) => f === p || f.startsWith(`${p}/`);
67	  }
68	  const source = p
69	    .split('/')
70	    .map((seg) =>
71	      seg === '**'
72	        ? STAR_STAR
73	        : seg.replace(ESCAPE_RE, '\\$&').replace(/\*/g, '[^/]*').replace(/\?/g, '[^/]'),
74	    )
75	    .join('/')
76	    // A leading `**/` matches ZERO or more directories — that's what makes
77	    // extension-test/**/*.test.js cover extension-test/host-policy.test.js too.
78	    .split(`${STAR_STAR}/`)
79	    .join('(?:.*/)?')
80	    .split(`/${STAR_STAR}`)
81	    .join('(?:/.*)?')
82	    .split(STAR_STAR)
83	    .join('.*');
84	  const re = new RegExp(`^${source}$`);
85	  return (f) => re.test(f);
86	}
87	
88	const matchers = (patterns) => patterns.map(toMatcher);
89	const anyMatch = (ms, file) => ms.some((m) => m(file));
90	
91	export default {
92	  id,
93	  severity,
94	  description: "package.json's test script globs reach every committed test file",
95	  doc,
96	  why,
97	
98	  run(ctx) {
99	    const raw = ctx.read('package.json');
100	    if (!raw) return [];
101	    let scripts;
102	    try {
103	      scripts = JSON.parse(raw).scripts || {};
104	    } catch {
105	      return []; // malformed package.json breaks npm first — not this check's finding
106	    }
107	
108	    const covered = matchers(runnerPatterns(scripts.test));
109	    if (!covered.length) return []; // no glob-driven `test` script — nothing to enforce
110	    const exempt = matchers(runnerPatterns(scripts['test:e2e']));
111	
112	    // ctx.files is the whole repo under the engine's default `all` sweep; a
113	    // --changed run narrows it, which only ever under-reports.
114	    return ctx.files
115	      .filter(isTestFile)
116	      .filter((f) => !anyMatch(covered, f) && !anyMatch(exempt, f))
117	      .map((file) => ({
118	        rule: id,
119	        severity,
120	        file,
121	        line: null,
122	        what: `${file} is reached by no pattern in package.json's \`test\` script`,
123	        why,
124	        fix:
125	          'add a glob covering it to the `test` script in package.json — or, if it is a heavy ' +
126	          'CI-only test, to `test:e2e` (which this check reads as the declared carve-out)',
127	        doc,
128	      }));
129	  },
130	};

2	name: testing-guide
3	description: Map of this repo's test suites, the requirements model, and where each harness documents itself. Use before writing or changing tests here, adding a requirement case, or debugging a suite — the invariants live in the gcec pack's RULES.md; this is the deeper how-to.
4	---
5	
6	# Testing in this repo
7	
8	```sh
9	npm install
10	npm run test:live      # integration: the REVIEWED assertions for each supported site
11	npm run test:offline   # unit: internal tests of the extraction logic
12	npm run test:ui        # UI: rendered popup/icon vs. the stored snapshot image
13	npm run refresh:ui     # regenerate snapshots after an intentional UI change
14	npm run test:e2e       # heavy: real Chrome, CI-only (skips without CHROME_PATH)
15	npm test               # everything above except e2e
16	```
17	
18	The invariants (mirror tree, reviewed-contract cases, `REFERENCE_NOW` floor) are
19	always-loaded in the gcec pack's RULES.md. General test discipline (see-it-fail,
20	refusal-test mutation, green-twice, high-watermark gating) is canon.
21	Adding a cached live case is covered under "Live integration tests" below; the
22	generic-coverage gate's invariants are in the gcec pack's RULES.md.
23	
24	## The requirements model — every leaf has exactly one case
25	
26	The spec (`dev/requirements/requirements.md`) is numbered prose; it does NOT
27	tag how a leaf is verified. Each leaf has exactly one
28	`<kind>/cases/<slug>.<id>.case.js` — the **filename** names the leaf, the
29	**folder** names the kind (the single classifier; no `kind` field, no side
30	manifest — issues #429/#435). `dev/requirements/shared/kinds.js` auto-discovers
31	kinds; adding one is a self-contained folder drop (`<kind>/kind.js`). The
32	kinds: **popup** (image, the popup's real `render()`), **icon** (image, the
33	real `toolbar-icon.js` in a fake browser), **behavior** (a click/navigation —
34	no image; verified by `dev/requirements/behavior/events-view-actions.test.js`),
35	**extractor** (per supported host, real extractor against a real cached page),
36	**logic** (product rules, executable `verify()`), plus `tbd: true` for a leaf
37	not yet faithfully verified. `dev/requirements/requirements-coverage.test.js`
38	fails unless every leaf has exactly one case (and rejects a typo'd/duplicate
39	case, an unknown kind, or a non-image case smuggling in a PNG). Full model +
40	how-to-add-one: `dev/requirements/README.md`.
41	
42	⚠️ The behavior test **stubs** `chrome.tabs.create`/`window.close` — every leaf
43	is *claimed*, not every leaf *faithfully* verified (#435; the banner in
44	`requirements.md` says the same).
45	
46	## Live integration tests
47	
48	`dev/requirements/extractor/live.test.js` is driven by declarative JSON in
49	`expected/`: `expected.events` is the **complete, exact** array the extractor
50	produces — deep-equal on `title`/`start`/`end`/`location`/`ctz`/`details`, no
51	matchers, array length included. The page URL lives **only** in
52	`data/server-fetched/<name>.url` (single source of truth — the recorder and the
53	test both read it; never in the case file). Tests run offline against the
54	committed cached HTML, loaded into a DOM at the `.url`'s URL so hostname
55	detection behaves exactly as in Chrome. `test.yml` never fetches.
56	
57	**Adding one.** Usually you don't: file an `extractor-request` issue with the
58	event URL and the `create-extractor` task records the page, writes the
59	extractor, and opens the PR. To add a case by hand, land the `.url` alone first
60	— a committed `.url` with no sibling `.html` *is* the request the `create-extractor`
61	task sweeps for, so it fetches the page (ScraperAPI; this sandbox is bot-blocked)
62	and opens a PR carrying it. Merge that, then run `npm run test:live` and paste
63	the printed values into `expected/<name>.json` — never hand-write them.
64	
65	**Gardening.** When an event page is taken down, point `<name>.url` at a newer
66	event **and delete the stale `<name>.html`** in the same commit; that is the
67	whole re-record request. Until an HTML file exists, `test:live` fails with
68	`Missing cached HTML for "<name>"`, so land the refresh before (or with) the
69	case's updated `expected`.
70	
71	## UI snapshots
72	
73	`dev/requirements/shared/render/visual-snapshots.test.js` renders each case and
74	pixel-compares (pixelmatch, `MAX_DIFF_RATIO = 0`) against the committed PNG.
75	`render-snapshot.js` picks the renderer by the case's folder: `popup/` → the
76	shipped `render()` path; `icon/` → the real `toolbar-icon.js` under
77	`fake-chrome.js`. Rasterizing is satori + resvg — **not a screenshot**: a
78	constrained flexbox subset that buys determinism with no browser; the renderer
79	folds the real `popup.css` onto the DOM as inline styles (one styling source of
80	truth). Snapshots are authored in **en-US** (a guard test enforces it). After
81	an intentional popup/view/CSS/icon change: `npm run refresh:ui`, commit the
82	PNGs + inline gallery. On mismatch the test writes `.actual.png`/`.diff.png`
83	under `dev/requirements/shared/.artifacts/` (gitignored) — and a moved baseline
84	goes through the snapshot-approval skill, never silent regeneration.
85	
86	## Where each harness documents itself
87	
88	The *why* of every non-obvious harness decision lives in that file's own
89	header/inline comments (the file-local-footgun rule) — read the file when you
90	touch it; this is just the map:
91	
92	- Generic-coverage gate — `dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage/generic-coverage.js`
93	  (field-by-field comparison) + `generic-coverage.test.js` (the high-watermark
94	  gate, #240).
95	- UI snapshot renderer limits (satori/resvg, CSS inlining, tall-list clamp,
96	  `skipRender`) — `dev/requirements/shared/render/popup-renderer.js`; the
97	  pixel-exact diff + en-US guard — `visual-snapshots.test.js`; gestures —
98	  `actions.js`.
99	- Behavior verification (stubbed boundary, self-asserting coverage) —
100	  `dev/requirements/behavior/events-view-actions.test.js`.
101	- Two-column gallery generator (managed `<!-- req-gallery:<id> -->` lines only;
102	  the file is part-authored, NOT on the `ours` driver) —
103	  `dev/requirements/shared/build-requirements-gallery.js`, gated by
104	  `dev/requirements/shared/requirements-gallery.test.js`.
105	- "Does the extension load?" — two layers:
106	  `extension-test/integration/extension-loads.test.js` (always-on, Chrome-faithful
107	  `importScripts`, #146) and `dev/requirements/heavy/extension-load.chrome.test.js`
108	  (real Chrome, verify via CI).
109	- Requirement numbering is parsed by `dev/requirements/shared/ui-requirements.js`
110	  (numbers only — it does NOT classify leaves).

2	name: snapshot-approval
3	description: Get owner approval for a moved UI-snapshot baseline. Use whenever a change to a dev/requirements case (its spec or its rendering) makes the snapshot tests fail — the pixels moved and the baseline wants to change.
4	---
5	
6	# Snapshot-approval process
7	
8	The general principle — a moved snapshot/golden baseline needs owner approval,
9	not silent regeneration — is canon. This is the project process when a change
10	to a `dev/requirements/<kind>/cases/*` case makes the snapshot tests **fail**:
11	
12	1. **Surface the diff immediately, don't carry on.** Revert the baseline to the
13	   committed **expected** PNG, run the snapshot test so it fails (the harness
14	   writes the rendered `actual` and a highlighted `diff` to
15	   `dev/requirements/shared/.artifacts/`), and send three images to the chat:
16	   **expected** (committed), **actual** (newly-rendered), and the **diff**.
17	   When the change alters the PNG's **dimensions** (e.g. a fixture shrink),
18	   pixelmatch can't diff unequal sizes so the harness writes only `actual` (no
19	   `diff`) — stitch **expected** and **actual** side-by-side into one image for
20	   the review instead.
21	2. **Ask via `AskUserQuestion`, not prose** — a popup notifies the owner on
22	   mobile. Offer **Approve** and **Reject — let's discuss**.
23	3. **Hold without overwriting the expected image.** If the working tree must be
24	   committed while waiting (e.g. a stop-hook), commit the *reverted* (expected)
25	   baseline so the branch/PR honestly shows the snapshot test **red, pending
26	   approval** — never commit the new baseline first.
27	4. On **Approve**: regenerate the baseline (`npm run refresh:ui`), confirm the
28	   suite is green, and push. On **Reject**: **do not** roll back automatically —
29	   leave the change in place and discuss how to proceed.

1	---
2	name: merge-and-ci
3	description: Drive this repo's PR-to-merged flow cheaply — when to open the PR, how to get CI green in a Claude web session, how to poll without wasting wall time or tokens, and when to arm auto-merge instead of waiting. Use whenever a session opens, watches, or lands a PR here — including one opened incidentally mid-task by an unattended or scheduled run, and any moment you ask "is CI green yet?" — not only for a deliberate merge or an e2e/heavy/UI change.
4	---
5	
6	# Merge and CI in this repo
7	
8	The merge itself: squash, `(#N)` appended to the title, CI green first (twice
9	for e2e/heavy-browser changes), approval-applies-only-backward — see the gcec
10	pack's RULES.md. This skill is the *how*: the environment facts and the poll
11	discipline that keep a merge cheap in wall time and tokens (from a post-mortem
12	on treating CI as a fixed poll-and-sleep ritual).
13	
14	## Open the PR early when the only reviewable output is on CI
15	
16	A change that adds or modifies an e2e/heavy-browser (`dev/requirements/heavy/`)
17	or UI-snapshot (`dev/requirements/{popup,icon}/`) test can't be exercised
18	locally — the sandbox has no Chrome — and its reviewable artifacts only exist
19	on a PR: CI runs the heavy/e2e suites against the branch, and a UI change's
20	reviewable output (the pixel diff GitHub renders, the inline gallery in the
21	branch's `dev/requirements/requirements.md`) needs a pushed branch to view at
22	all. Open the PR early for those.
23	
24	## Getting a green check in a Claude web session
25	
26	- **The push-run exists — don't dispatch a duplicate.** A push through the
27	  in-session git proxy **does** trigger `test.yml`: the workflow's `push`
28	  trigger covers `main` and `claude/**` precisely so an agent branch gets CI
29	  without a PR, and a branch that also has an open PR gets a `pull_request` run
30	  too (two `test` check runs on the same head SHA — the workflow's own comment
31	  calls that accepted duplication). Merge on whichever is green; only reach for
32	  `actions_run_trigger` / `run_workflow` when no run appeared at all (a branch
33	  outside `claude/**`, or a `paths-ignore`/`[skip ci]` push). Firing a manual
34	  dispatch on top of a run that already exists just buys a third run and its
35	  wall time.
36	- **The shell can't observe GitHub state here.** The git remote is a git-only
37	  proxy (smart-HTTP under `/git/<owner>/<repo>/…`; every other path 400s),
38	  there's no API token in the env, and `gh` reaches no `api.github.com` — only
39	  an MCP poll sees check state; a background bash/Monitor loop cannot.
40	- **Poll on a short back-off, never one long sleep, never tight.** Loop
41	  **MCP poll → background sleep → MCP poll** until the check leaves
42	  `in_progress`, backing off **5s, 10s, 15s, 30s, then 30s** repeating — a
43	  fast run wakes you within seconds, a slow one isn't tight-polled. Always wait
44	  for the sleep's completion notification before the next poll. While a sleep
45	  runs, do real work (review the diff, draft the PR body) or end the turn —
46	  filler calls to look busy are tight-polling in disguise.
47	- **Don't reach for `subscribe_pr_activity` to wait for green** — its webhooks
48	  never deliver CI **success** (only failures/comments/reviews), so the
49	  transition you're waiting for never arrives. It's for babysitting a PR, not
50	  merge-on-green.
51	- **Won't sit and poll to green? Arm auto-merge — never end a turn on a
52	  subscription.** A run that opens a PR it can't watch to the end (an
53	  unattended/scheduled run, or a fix opened incidentally mid-task) should
54	  `enable_pr_auto_merge` with `SQUASH` and finish: this repo's
55	  `maintenance.delivery` is `auto-merge`, so GitHub lands it the moment the
56	  checks pass, with no turn held open and no human in the loop. Ending the turn
57	  "waiting for CI events" instead strands the PR until a person notices —
58	  measured, in session `558026a0` (2026-07-24): both `test` runs were green at
59	  03:58:27Z, the turn had ended at 03:57:56Z on a `subscribe_pr_activity` watch,
60	  and PR #718 sat unmerged until the owner stepped in **63 minutes** later.
61	  That one avoidable wait was 85% of the session's 74-minute wall clock.
62	- **…but expect the arming itself to be refused here, and read the refusal as
63	  state, not as failure.** On this repo's single required `test` check,
64	  `enable_pr_auto_merge` has essentially no window: while the run is queued or
65	  `in_progress` GitHub refuses *"unstable status (required checks are
66	  failing)"*, and the moment it completes green it refuses *"already in clean
67	  status … you can merge directly."* Neither is an error to escalate — the
68	  first means poll on the back-off above and retry, the second means the merge

input.body:
Weekly **prose-to-checks sweep** over `.claudinite/local/packs` (the `gcec` pack), for #860 (slot `w2026-08-09`). One conversion.

## The rule converted

The testing-guide skill's "Live integration tests" rule: *the page URL lives **only** in `dev/requirements/extractor/data/<provenance>/<name>.url` — the single source of truth the recorder writes and `live.test.js` reads — **never in the case file**.*

**Why it needed a mechanism.** The violation is inert, so nothing goes red. `live.test.js` reads exactly three keys off a case object (`description`, `referenceNow`, `expected`) and resolves the URL from the sibling `.url`; any other key is silently ignored. A `"url"` in `expected/<name>.json` — the natural thing to write when hand-authoring a case — is never read, never asserted, never printed, and goes stale the first time gardening re-points the `.url` at a newer event. It then misleads the next reader of the reviewed contract about which page the assertions came from.

## The check

`case-url-single-source` (blocking) — `.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/case-url-single-source.mjs`, registered in `pack.mjs`.

It **parses** each `expected/*.json` and reports any url-shaped *key* (`url`, `pageUrl`, `source_url`, …), naming its path (`expected.events[0].sourceUrl`) and the line to delete.

Parsing rather than grepping is the whole point of this one: every committed case's `details` field opens with the link back to the source page (that is what `buildCalendarUrl` puts in the `details=` param), so a text search for a URL reports **all 36 cases** and is useless. Only a url-shaped key is the violation, which is why no string value is ever inspected — `details`, `location` and `description` may all legitimately contain a URL.

## Proof

- **See-it-fail is on the record**: the fixtures were written against a stub returning `[]`, and both "fires" tests failed on violating input before the implementation landed.
- Fixtures cover both firing directions (top-level and nested, with the offending line number) and four quiet cases: the real committed case shape, the `.url` file itself, non-case JSON, a merely url-*ish* key name (`"urls in the blurb"`), and unparseable JSON (which `test:live` already fails loudly on — not double-reported here).
- `npm test`: **546 tests, 0 failing** (8 skipped — the Chrome-dependent ones).
- Run against the live repo tree the new rule yields **0 findings**. `check_the_world.mjs` is unchanged by this PR: its 4 blocking findings are the pre-existing `product-wiki-page-sections` ones, out of this sweep's scope.

## Prose: no deletion

The deletion test was applied and says **keep the paragraph whole**. Beside the URL rule it also carries the deep-equal contract, the offline/DOM-at-the-`.url`'s-hostname mechanics, and "`test.yml` never fetches" — none of which the check covers, and the test trims nothing.

## Candidates considered and left as prose

- **The `extension-test/` mirror-tree invariant** — a static signature, but it does not hold on today's tree in either direction (a dozen sources have no mirror test; `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js` has no mirrored source), so no confident fixture exists. Left as prose.
- **"All page fetching goes through `scraperapi.mjs`"** — `prepare.mjs` legitimately `fetch()`es the GitHub API, and no static signature separates "a page fetch" from "an API fetch". Left as prose.
- **The workflow-failure-classification gap** — this repo currently has no `workflow_run` / `repository_dispatch` workflow at all, so the rule has no subject to prove a check against.

Not auto-merged — this task's outcome ceiling is `open-pr`, and a check can misfire, so it wants owner review.
